home.pillarsSubtitle: Not a loud skin keyboard—an input tool that aims for system-like feel while keeping RIME depth.
home.pillar1Body: Layout, feedback, and candidates stay close to the iOS keyboard. Full QWERTY and Chinese nine-key are product work—not a reskin.
home.pillar2Body: Composition and candidates are handled locally by default. No ads, no selling data. Full Access is explained and purpose-bound.
home.pillar3Body: Schemes such as rime-ice, fuzzy pinyin, user dictionaries, and configurable behavior—desktop RIME ideas under iOS constraints.
home.showcaseBody: The main app stays Settings-like; the extension follows native keyboard rhythm and readability. Screenshots and video will replace these placeholders.
home.trustTitle: Third-party keyboards need trust up front
home.trust1Body: No cross-app tracking. The keyboard is not an ad surface.
home.trust2Body: Used for shared configuration, local dictionaries, and optional features—not to upload keystrokes.
home.trust3Body: Core project code is MIT. Upstream RIME and scheme licenses are documented in-app and here.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: System-like feel and RIME configurability on one product line.

items.title: Near-native keyboard chrome
items.body: System-gray surfaces, high-contrast keys, stable hit targets—usability over decoration.

items.title: Full keyboard & Chinese nine-key
items.body: Both layouts are treated as product surfaces. Nine-key aligns with system-style letter groups and path selection.

items.title: Candidates and paths
items.body: Candidate bar and nine-key pinyin paths prioritize readability and touch accuracy with low visual noise.

items.title: librime + librime-lua
items.body: Production path uses pinned RIME artifacts and a clear bridge layer between engine and UI.

items.title: Scheme management
items.body: Deploy and manage schemes in the main app; the extension focuses on session input, not heavy deployment.

items.title: Fuzzy pinyin & dictionaries
items.body: Configurable fuzzy pinyin and local user-dictionary paths so input adapts to how you type.

items.title: Typing intelligence (optional)
items.body: Off by default. When enabled, only aggregate stats stay on device—original text is not kept.

items.title: Correction with bounds
items.body: Correction and related learning are bounded and clearable; host context is not quietly exported.

items.title: Configurable feedback
items.body: Sound and haptics stay under your control in settings.

items.title: Extension does not ship keystrokes
items.body: It does not upload unfinished composition, candidates, clipboard, or host identity to the developer.

items.title: Optional settings sync
items.body: RIME settings sync only after you choose a destination; sensitive profiles can leave the device encrypted by design.

items.title: Standard RIME sync
items.body: With explicit confirmation, dictionary snapshots can interoperate with compatible RIME frontends—separate from the input path.

getStarted.title: Get started
getStarted.subtitle: Third-party keyboards must be enabled in system settings. Follow these steps for first setup.
getStarted.note: Labels vary by iOS version. Screenshots will be added when assets are ready.

steps.title: Install the app
steps.body: Install Universe Keyboard from the App Store (when available) and open the main app once to finish basic onboarding.

steps.title: Add the keyboard
steps.body: Go to Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard… and choose Universe Keyboard.

steps.title: Allow Full Access if needed
steps.body: If you need shared configuration, local dictionary learning, or other documented optional capabilities, allow Full Access. You can revoke it anytime in system settings.

steps.title: Deploy an input scheme
steps.body: Return to the main app and install/deploy a RIME scheme (e.g. rime-ice resources) until status is ready.

steps.title: Switch keyboards in any app
steps.body: While typing, hold the globe key or use the keyboard switcher and select Universe Keyboard.

faqs.a: To read the shared container prepared by the main app, settings, and local resources. The design is not to upload your keystrokes. See the privacy policy.

faqs.q: Do you upload what I type?
faqs.a: The keyboard extension does not send input to developer servers for analytics or ads. Optional sync only happens after you configure it, within documented categories.

faqs.q: How is this different from the system Chinese keyboard?
faqs.a: It aims for a similar quiet feel while offering RIME schemes, layouts, and configurable input behavior.

about.title: About Universe Keyboard
about.subtitle: Bringing familiar RIME power to a nearer-native iOS third-party keyboard.
about.storyBody: The system keyboard is excellent—and many people still need configurable pinyin schemes, nine-key habits, or the RIME ecosystem. Universe Keyboard is not a louder skin. It tries to deliver quiet, usable, configurable input inside iOS sandbox and extension limits.
stack: KeyboardCore logic layer with a clear bridge boundary
about.licenseBody: Project code is MIT. RIME/librime is BSD-3-Clause; OpenCC is Apache-2.0. Schemes such as rime-ice may be GPL-3.0—read and accept in-app terms before use.
